# RF Sentinel

> Free, open-source (GPL-3.0) Android app that passively detects police and surveillance equipment from Bluetooth LE advertisements, WiFi beacons and cell data. No root, no Termux, no account, no analytics. Android 8.0+. Signed APK on GitHub Releases. Receive-only: it never transmits to or connects to scanned devices.

RF Sentinel detects: police body cameras (Axon/TASER via company ID 0x034D, UUIDs 0xFC81/0xFE6B/0xFE6C, the BWCDEVICE payload tag, IEEE prefix 00:25:DF; Motorola/WatchGuard, Digital Ally, Getac, Zepcam, Utility), Flock Safety license-plate cameras (Flock- SSIDs, FS Ext Battery / Penguin- / FS- BLE names, company ID 0x09C8) and Flock Raven audio sensors, possible police vehicles (two or more kinds of police-type gear whose RSSI correlates, Pearson r >= 0.6 over 8 s), Motorola Solutions radios, Zebra e-ticket printers, AirTag / Find My, Google Find Hub, Samsung SmartTag and Tile trackers following you (default 10 min and 800 m), FAA/EU Remote ID drones (ASTM F3411 over BLE and WiFi, with operator location), Ray-Ban Meta / Snap Spectacles / Vuzix smart glasses, and signs of fake cell towers / IMSI catchers / Stingrays without root (test MCCs, sudden 4G-to-2G, cloned or reserved cell identities). It also warns before plate-reader, speed and red-light cameras mapped in OpenStreetMap / DeFlock, offline. It runs on Android Auto and can use ESP32 boards running OUI-Spy or GhostESP.

Related tools and how RF Sentinel compares (Flock You, OUI-Spy / OUI-APEX, Wardrive Go, Fieldwatch, Flock-You for Android, AirGuard, BLE Radar, Rayhunter) are covered in the Q&A. It is a free alternative to SØPHIA (s0phia ops / SophiaOps), which is a paid Termux-based tool. RF Sentinel is independent and not affiliated with SØPHIA or DetecX.
